svg.title: Anatomy of a Delta Table on OneLake for Microsoft Fabric
svg.desc: A rich visual infographic showing the physical and logical anatomy of a Delta table in OneLake: OneLake unified storage layer, Lakehouse workspace path, Transaction Log (_delta_log JSON commits, checkpoints, optimistic concurrency race), Actual Data (Parquet files, partition folders, V-Order compression), Fabric compute engine access, and Plain Parquet vs Delta Table comparison.
svg.text: ANATOMY OF A DELTA TABLE ON ONELAKE FOR MICROSOFT FABRIC
Cross-tenant, Distributed Object Store (ADLS Gen2 Foundation)

g.title: _delta_log: numbered JSON commits — Each commit is a zero-padded, sequentially numbered JSON file recording add/remove actions.
Checkpoint (every 10 commits) — The log is periodically folded into a Parquet checkpoint so metadata reads stay fast.
Optimistic concurrency: atomic commit race — Only one writer wins a given commit number; the loser detects the collision and retries.
g.text: • Writers stage Parquet files independently with zero global locks.
• Atomic rename on OneLake determines single winner; loser retries at N+1.

g.title: Immutable Parquet data objects — The physical rows of the table, stored as immutable Parquet files.
Snapshot-isolated read — A reader pins to the newest fully-committed log record at query start and never sees later writes.
g.text: Readers pin to latest commit ID at query start; concurrent writers never cause dirty reads.
Historical time travel available via VERSION AS OF or timestamp replay.

g.title: Trap: unhandled commit collisions — A writer that doesn't retry on collision fails outright instead of safely reattempting.
g.text: Trap: Unhandled Commit Collisions in Custom Clients
Writers must implement atomic rename conflict detection and retry at N+1 commit ID.
Always use standard Spark or Delta-rs connectors with exponential backoff retries.

svg.text: Fabric Codex — Original Infographic, August 2026. Sourced from Delta Lake Architecture & OneLake Storage Specification.
